descriptionChirho: Qal: an event comes to pass or befalls someone, used of circumstances, fate, or incidents that take place — often with pronominal suffix indicating the affected person
Qal with personal object: to meet or encounter someone directly, focusing on the experiential contact between persons rather than an impersonal event befalling
Nifal (reflexive/reciprocal): to meet one another, come upon someone, or be encountered — the standard Hebrew stem for expressing mutual or deliberate meeting
Hifil (causative): to cause something to happen or to designate/select — includes appointing cities of refuge (causing the fugitive to 'encounter' sanctuary) and causing events to come about
